title: LF Repair Dynamic V3 — adaptive repair selection and multi-front closure
primary_question: Does dynamic signal-driven selection of diagnostic modules, reasoning strategies and repair operators improve durable multi-front repair quality without increasing false-positive closure or unjustified cost?

selection_evaluation.rule: selection is judged from case evidence and material problem signals, never by family label
wrong_selection: selected strategy has no triggering signal/evidence
material signal exists but required module is skipped without justified containment
escalates to expensive search when deterministic repair is already established
uses direct repair while competing material causes remain
creates capability when existing governed composition is sufficient

efficiency_rule.quality_precedence: efficiency may not trade away material evidence
efficiency_rule.telemetry: use measured live telemetry only; never estimate missing provider tokens/latency

automatic_reject_if: source benchmark or frozen variant mutated
material front omission causes false closure
candidate_preferred_if: root-cause and repair quality are non-regressive against the best comparator
material-front coverage and second-order detection improve on cases where those apply
selector avoids unnecessary expensive reasoning on deterministic cases
no unjustified new architecture/capability authority is introduced

notes: The 82 visible cases are inherited exactly from V2 so changes are attributable to method behavior.
V3 does not cancel or rewrite V2; V2 remains historical evidence.
Additional selector-specific holdouts may be added only as a separate frozen extension, never silently appended after V3 starts.
